title: How much copper does one zinc make?
hook: Drop zinc into blue copper solution and copper metal appears. Count the trade.

knows: that metals can corrode or dissolve
that an ion is a charged atom
doesNotKnow: that in these reactions electrons move from one particle to another in matched numbers
that losing electrons is called oxidation and gaining them reduction

misconception: Oxidation always means adding oxygen, or electrons appear and vanish, so the numbers need not match.
objective: The learner can explain that each zinc atom gives 2 electrons and each Cu²⁺ ion takes 2, so one copper atom forms for each zinc atom that dissolves, because electrons only move and are never made or lost.

claims.text: Zinc metal in a copper(II) solution dissolves as Zn²⁺ while copper metal forms: Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu.
claims.source: Standard displacement reaction; E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V, E°(Zn²⁺/Zn) = −0.76 V (CRC Handbook, 'Electrochemical series'), so the reaction is spontaneous. Copper(II) sulfate solution is blue.

claims.text: Each zinc atom gives away 2 electrons and each Cu²⁺ ion takes 2 electrons to become a copper atom, so one copper atom forms per zinc atom.
claims.source: Half-reactions Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻ and Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu; charge balance gives 1:1 (Atkins & Jones, Chemical Principles, ch. on electrochemistry). Demo.tsx PER = 2 for both.

claims.text: Electrons are not made or lost in a chemical reaction; they only move from one particle to another.
claims.source: Conservation of charge; redox as electron transfer (IUPAC Gold Book, 'oxidation', 'reduction').

claims.text: Losing electrons is called oxidation; gaining them is called reduction.
claims.source: IUPAC Gold Book, 'oxidation' (removal of electrons) and 'reduction' (gain of electrons).

claims.text: The stage moves electrons one at a time; in real solution the half-way Cu⁺ step is not something you would see, and the two electrons arrive at the metal surface.
claims.source: Cu⁺ is unstable in water and disproportionates (Greenwood & Earnshaw, Chemistry of the Elements, ch. 28); the electron-at-a-time display is a teaching device, recorded here so the stage's 'Cu⁺' label is not read as a claim about the mechanism.

recall.question: An aluminium atom gives away 3 electrons (Al → Al³⁺). Silver ions, Ag⁺, each need 1. Per aluminium atom, how many silver atoms form?
recall.why: Electrons only move: 3 given must be 3 taken, and each Ag⁺ takes 1, so 3 silver atoms per aluminium atom.
